title: When the Berezin transform fails to detect compactness: Toeplitz operators with $L^1$ symbols on weighted Bergman spaces
summary: For every $n\geq1$ and $γ>-1$, we construct $f\in L^1(\mathbb B_n,dv_γ)$ whose Toeplitz form extends to a bounded, noncompact operator on the weighted Bergman spaces $A^2_γ(\mathbb B_n)$ and whose Berezin transform vanishes at the boundary. Boundary vanishing of the Berezin transform therefore does not imply compactness for Toeplitz operators with integrable symbols, in contrast with operators in the Toeplitz algebra generated by bounded symbols; this answers a question of Bauer and Isralowitz.
